sentences.text:
15.11.2023 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
01.

1. Heard Mr. A. Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Addl. Govt.
Advocate for the State.
2.

This is an application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the petitioner in connection with Khantapada P.S. Case No. 129 of 2023 corresponding to Special Case No. 154 of 2023 pending in the Court of the learned A.D.J. -cum- Special Court under POCSO Act, Balasore, Odisha registered for commission of offences punishable under Sections 376-AB, 506 of IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
3. The petitioner had moved an application for bail before the Court of learned A.D.J. -cum- Special Court under POCSO Act, Balasore which was rejected on 01.11.2023.

4. The prosecution allegation in brief is that on 25.05.2023 while the grand daughter had been to shop of the petitioner to purchase chocolates and Kurkure, the petitioner asked her to go to his house to get those items.

In his house the petitioner undressed the victim girl and rubbed his private part on the private part of the victim girl, the victim cried, the mother of the petitioner came there and the petitioner left the victim girl but threatened her not to disclose such things to anyone otherwise he would kill her entire family.
FIR was lodged after five days of the occurrence.

5. Mr. A. Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 01.06.2023 and trial has started in the case and the victim has also been examined during trial for which there is no apprehension of the petitioner tampering with any prosecution evidence, if he is released on bail.
He further submits that the delay of five days in lodging of the FIR has not been Ajay Kumar Behera vs State Of Odisha & Another .....

sentences.text:
Opp. ... on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180489719/
1 explained and false allegations have been made against the petitioner as he has a grocery shop in the village and there is a dispute between the family of the victim and the petitioner regarding payment of his dues.
His alternate submission is that the petitioner may be granted interim bail for a period of three months and he undertakes to abide any condition which may be imposed for releasing him on bail.
Learned counsel for the petitioner files a memo along with the copy of the FIR.
The same is taken on record.

6. Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Addl. Govt. Advocate for the State opposed the prayer for bail stating that the allegations against the petitioner which are there in the FIR has been supported by the victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as in her evidence recorded during the trial.
As the allegation is being heinous in nature, the petitioner does not deserve to be released on bail.

7. Considering the nature of allegations against the petitioner and as the case is in the midst of trial,
I am not inclined to allow the prayer for bail.

The BLAPL is accordingly dismissed,
8.
It is open to the petitioner to move the learned Court below for interim bail if so advised, which shall be considered in accordance with law.
9. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
(Savitri Ratho) Judge Sukanta Signed by: SUKANTA KUMAR BEHERA
